visualStyleNotes: Anatomy Atelier quality bar throughout: warm off-white studio backdrop, no floor grid, no glow, no bloom, no emissive materials, no cartoon outlines. The road is a long warm ivory low wall (like a museum timeline display) running along X from x=0 to x=30, with eight planet spheres on short posts at distance-appropriate heights. The AU ruler is a thin amber-grey line floating just above the road, carrying small tick planes. The light-time counter is a small readout panel that travels along the ruler, showing minutes flown since the Sun. The asteroid belt appears as hundreds of tiny neutral stone spheres clustered across the belt zone. Planet colors are the branch's muted set; everything reads diagrammatic, not cartoonish.
materialNotes: Metallic-roughness PBR, metallic=0, roughness ~0.6-0.7 matte throughout. Road: warm ivory with faint fill-line detail. Posts: warm grey slim cylinders. Planet spheres: baked mottling/banding, no image textures. Belt stones: small low-poly rock spheres in warm grey-browns. Ruler: thin flat amber-grey strip with dark tick marks. Counter: dark text sprite on ivory panel. No emissive channels.
assetBrief: SUBJECT: A linear distance timeline along X: 0 AU at x=0 to 30 AU at x=30. Distance scale: 1 AU = 1.0 scene unit exactly, so the road is 30 units long. Sun post at x=0 (radius 0.4, on a 0.15-tall base). Planet posts at their true relative X: Mercury 0.39, Venus 0.72, Earth 1.0, Mars 1.52, Jupiter 5.2, Saturn 9.58, Uranus 19.2, Neptune 30.0. Sphere display radii are consistent with the size component (Earth 0.24, Mercury 0.09 … Jupiter 2.64) but capped at 0.9 scene units to keep the road readable, each on a low post (height ∝ radius so taller worlds don't hog the ruler). The AU ruler: thin strip at y=0.75 above the road, ticks every 1 AU, numbered 0 … 30, with the 1 AU tick marked 'home'. Asteroid belt band: hundreds of small grey spheres scattered over the road between x=2.1 and 5.1 (the zone where the visual belt lives in this projection). Light-time counter: a small panel that can be 'played' — it advances along the road at light speed (about 0.3 AU per second at max zoom out) showing 'Sun light has reached Mars — 12 min 40 s' style messages, and stops at each planet with the time spent reaching it (Mercury 3.2 min, Venus 6 min, Earth 8.3 min, Mars 12.6 min, Jupiter 43.3 min, Saturn 79 min, Uranus 160 min, Neptune 250 min — approximate rounded numbers, presented as approximate). Default camera starts near the inner road [0.6, 1.3, 3.1] → [2.2, 0.1, 0]; dragging/scroll camera moves along the road; a 'tour' button animates the camera from x=0 to x=30 and back. Grounding: radial ground-shadow beneath the whole road strip, plus the ivory road band itself is the primary grounding. Named groups per layers list.
